narrative.overview:
The game is the dancefloor: a PixiJS arena whose shader pulses, shakes and changes palette with the music. Every React screen the player meets is a pane of smoked glass laid over that floor and lit by it. Panels are translucent floor black with a faint white hairline and a backdrop blur, so the level keeps moving through them. Even the landing page plays a live level behind its copy, with a silent demo of shots landing on the kick.

Behind the glass is the booth, where the sound is made. The sound playground (`/playground`) is a bass synth's front panel in the same palette: opaque Console Grey slabs framed in rows, Floor Black wells and screens set into them, arc knobs, small square latches and curve screens whose handles you drag. It is dense, flat and labelled like gear. The floor and the booth share one palette, one type pair and one rule for light; they differ in material (glass over a live game, opaque panel around a tool) and in shape (pills on the floor, square latches in the booth).

The chrome recedes and the game leads. Color and glow are not decoration. They mark state: the slot you're holding, a magazine that's loaded, a combo, dash being ready, a heart you just got back, the engine that's armed. The one deliberate performance is the wordmark: heavy italic caps in a violet-to-blue gradient, RIDDIM stacked over RIOT, whose O is the level's circle filling a quarter on each beat at 140 BPM. Density runs high in the HUD and the booth (small mono readouts, segment bars, key caps, knobs) and loose on the landing and level cards, where a single headline holds the screen.

The system rejects two neighbours. It is not generic SaaS, so no bland blue-pill-on-white app feel and no settings-form arrangement of a tool, even though it starts from a stock token set. And it is not cyberpunk cliché: no glitch text, scanlines or magenta/cyan hacker styling. It is dark only; light surfaces never appear.
keyCharacteristics: Smoked glass panels (70-75% floor black, 12% white hairline, 6-8px blur) over the live game
Opaque synth-panel slabs in the booth: Console Grey rows with Floor Black wells, screens and latches set into them
Glow means state: an active, ready, armed or rewarded element gets a soft colored halo; resting elements get none
Mono uppercase, widely tracked labels in UV Violet name each panel and section
In the booth, Strobe Blue is the sound design and Hype Amber is the auditioned weapon's own values, never the other way round
One loud moment per screen: the wordmark, a level heading or the combo
Motion keyed to the tempo, and switched off when flashing is reduced

rules.name: The Glow Is State Rule
rules.body: A colored halo (`0 0 14px` at 50-55% of the color, or `0 0 8px` at 55% on a small dot) or a `currentColor` drop-shadow appears only on an element that is active, ready, armed or rewarded. A resting element never glows.

rules.name: The One Job Per Light Rule
rules.body: Each accent keeps its meaning across every screen: blue is yours and ready, violet names things and marks drops, amber is reward, coral is health and danger. Don't borrow an accent for decoration.

rules.name: The Design Blue, Weapon Amber Rule
rules.body: Wherever the sound design and one rolled weapon are edited side by side, Strobe Blue is the design (the values every weapon shares, and the page's own state) and Hype Amber is only the weapon being auditioned (its roll and its overrides). A control that edits the design is never amber; a control that edits only this weapon is never blue. Test: cover the labels, and the colour alone still tells you whether a change will be saved to the game.

rules.name: The Dark Floor Rule
rules.body: Every surface is dark. The theme's light mode tokens exist but are never shown (the color mode is forced to dark), so never design for them.

rules.name: The Gear Voice Rule
rules.body: Anything technical (a key, a BPM, a seed, a count, a key binding, a parameter and its value) is set in mono. Prose is never set in mono.

rules.name: The Tabular Numbers Rule
rules.body: Live numbers (score, combo, stats, knob readouts, curve captions, meter scale) use `font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` so they don't jitter as they change.

rules.name: The Glass Not Paper Rule
rules.body: Panels over the game are translucent and blurred, never opaque cards with drop shadows. The only opaque surface over play is the overlay panel, which freezes it. (The booth is not over the game; its opaque slabs hold the game in a window instead.)

rules.name: The Recess Rule
rules.body: In the booth, a panel is lighter than the page and everything you read or touch inside it is darker than the panel. Nothing in the booth is raised above its slab except the dropdown.

dos: Do build every in-game panel as glass: Floor Black at 70-75%, a 1px Haze White hairline at 12%, a 6-8px backdrop blur.
Do build booth tools as opaque Console Grey slabs with Floor Black screens, wells and latches set into them, framed rows split by 1px Floor Black dividers.
Do spend glow only on state (active, ready, armed, reward), with the 14px halo, the 8px dot halo or a `currentColor` drop-shadow.
Do keep each accent to its one job: Strobe Blue yours/ready, UV Violet labels/drops, Hype Amber reward, Alarm Coral health/danger.
Do colour every booth control by what it edits: Strobe Blue for the sound design and page state, Hype Amber for the auditioned weapon's roll and overrides.
Do mark a moved value against its reference: the Smoke Grey tick on the knob ring, a Strobe Blue Bright readout, and a Reset that only enables once something moved.
Do name panels and sections with a mono uppercase UV Violet label (0.75rem; 0.2em tracking on the floor, 0.16em in the booth).
Do set keys, numbers, seeds, BPM and parameter values in mono, with tabular numbers for anything live.
Do draw what a value does (a curve screen with draggable handles) where a slider list would hide it, and give every handle a knob for the keyboard.
Do time looping motion to the tempo (a beat at 140 BPM is ~0.43s).
Do stop every looping or popping animation under `:root[data-flashing='reduced']`, and keep new canvas flashes and shake inside the stage's `calmFrame`.
Do add `env(safe-area-inset-*)` to fixed edge controls, and give touch targets at least the design system's minimum target (44px on touch).
donts: Don't introduce light surfaces or light-mode variants; the color mode is forced dark.
Don't use glitch text, scanlines, RGB-split type or magenta/cyan hacker styling.
Don't let a screen read like a SaaS app: no opaque white-ish cards, no stock dashboard chrome, no settings-form stack of slider lists, no more than one primary pill per screen.
Don't put opaque, shadowed cards over the live game; only the pause/end overlay is opaque.
Don't colour a design control amber or a weapon-only control blue.
Don't put a kicker or eyebrow label above a heading; the heading speaks for itself.
Don't add a second loud moment to a screen that already has the wordmark, a level heading or the combo.
Don't lay out a page as a row of equal cards; group by meaning on one surface instead.
Don't re-render React per frame for a meter or playhead; draw onto the elements from an animation frame.
Don't hard-code a color or size outside the theme; use `theme.color()`, `theme.spacing()` and `theme.fontSize()` so the scale and modes stay one source.
